correctness.rationale: With n≥4, remove s≥1 disjoint edges from K_n and set H_α=(1−α)I−α M+αJ. Matched-difference eigendirections have eigenvalue 1−2α; α<1/2 gives H_α positive definite and unique positive equilibrium paired x=c/(1−2α), unmatched c/(1−α), c=[1+α(2s/(1−2α)+r/(1−α))]^-1. The Volterra relative-entropy Lyapunov derivative −(x−x*)ᵀH_α(x−x*) proves global convergence. At α=1/2 the equal-twin simplex and pair-ratio first integrals yield the stated critical proportions on the pair-balanced manifold. For 1/2<α<1, invasion-rate exclusion and transverse positive splitting eigenvalues leave exactly the one-pair equilibria stable. On pair-balanced trajectories, d log(q_i/q_j)/dt=(2α−1)(q_i−q_j), so the unique initially largest pair is selected; with s=1 the extinct twin and unmatched-only equilibria cannot attract strictly positive starts. Finite potential and isolated equilibria yield the convergence claim. Independent 63 rational identity/eigenvalue checks passed.
residual_risks: The one-pair winner law is asserted only for 1/2<α<1 and pair-balanced starts with a unique largest pair, except s=1 where all strictly positive starts are allowed.
Critical manifold includes boundary points, but claim does not classify all possible boundary equilibria at α=1/2.

originality.rationale: Mooij et al. These do not furnish a family-wide K_n-minus-arbitrary-matching phase diagram, the α=1/2 neutral simplex, or initial-ratio winner selection. Some low-order special cases and standard symmetric LV Lyapunov methods are covered prior work. A general complete-multipartite theorem may implicitly specialize; none was located in the bounded primary comparison.

value.rationale: Deleting a vanishing fraction 1/binom(n,2) of competitive edges yet halving the full-coexistence threshold for all n is a sharp robustness discontinuity in a natural ecological network family. The explicit neutral phase and exact deterministic winner-selection mechanism add structural dynamical content beyond routine spectrum calculation, and future work on near-complete interaction graphs can use the full characterization.
residual_risks: Heterogeneous interaction strengths and postcritical α≥1 are outside scope.

final_claim: For homogeneous symmetric competitive Lotka–Volterra on K_n minus any nonempty matching, stable full coexistence ends exactly at α=1/2 (versus α=1 on K_n); at criticality there is a pair simplex and above it an explicit balanced-start winner rule for 1/2<α<1.
limitations: Stable states classified only for α<1; winner selection requires pair balance and a unique leading pair except when s=1.
No heterogeneity, stochasticity, or dynamic graph modifications.
